title: Drumstick types, woods and prices, then and now
summary: Compares old military sticks with modern plastic-tipped ones; pine, maple and hickory; price per pair; early lack of wire brushes.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: A question about drumsticks. Of course, you made drumsticks, but you were familiar with what drumsticks looked like at that time. Around the time that you were leaving home, were the drumsticks that were used by drummers larger than they are used now, or, say, the drumsticks that you have now...
Yeah, a little... The drumsticks that they used then was...what you call it...? Military drums, that you use in...
Military.
Yeah, military drums. They didn't use the kind of sticks that we use now. In fact, they didn't make them. What they use now is the plastic tips...
That's right.
Plastic tips. And some is not plastic. The ones that's not plastic, they'll split. You've got a... To the end you've got a (?) with a splinter...what'cha call
Moore (I) - 17
them, splinter...? Like a little chip get in them. I see.
But the plastic don't do that. The plastic sticks, they don't split. They would end up breaking. Finally, in the end, in the (?), it will break. But they won't split.
I see. Do you prefer these plastic tipped drumsticks today as opposed to...?
Yes. Plastic sticks is better. You get a very...a crisp roll. But you got to know how to roll.
Sure. Well, we'll get into some of those things as we go along. What were the sticks years ago made of, when you were a youngster first starting out at the drums?

Pine wood and maple -- maple wood. Some was made out of hickory, hickory wood. But you can't...you can't... It's hard to find. You can't find the hickory sticks no more. The ordinary sticks now that I use cost $3.50 or $4 a pair. If you have the hickory stick, it will cost you round about $6 a pair, $7.

And I didn't know anything about wire brushes during that time. You didn't use no wire brushes. I come to New York, they were using the wire brushes. The wire brushes cost you a dollar and a half a pair during that time. Now
Moore (I) - 18
the same wire brush (they may make them a little bit better; I don't know) can run you from four to five dollars, six dollars a pair, right now.
You gave the prices for drumsticks now. Years ago, what would pine sticks cost?
Fifty cents a pair.
Fifty cents a pair. The rate of inflation.
[CHUCKLES]

Which did you find... Of course, all the drummers had their preferences. Some would like the pine and others would like the hickory. Were there any of the wood types, maple or hickory or pine, that were more popular than others?
Well...
Or was it simply a matter of individual preference all the way down?
Pine wood was... It's a light fit.
It's light.
And the maple sticks is next to it. It's light, too. And the hickory sticks, forget about that -- you couldn't get those at all.
